messages:
liz: Heads-up — console is showing quota 'flaps' for a small set of tenants after the new client runtime shipped this morning. Dashboards spike then drop repeatedly over ~5m windows.
raj: Seen that. Any correlation with route headers or policy changes? looks like attribution switching between route variants
mike: I pulled the edge logs — requests from the TS client are sending an extra header `X-Client-RouteHint` when retries kick in. Server treats it as a different route and attributes to a different quota bucket.
liz: exact example from logs:
```
POST /v1/generate 200 15ms tenant=acme route=nlp-v2 X-Client-RouteHint: narrowcast
POST /v1/generate 200 18ms tenant=acme route=nlp-v2 X-Client-RouteHint: default
```
Same token, same session, but two distinct route hints, so console split the burn between two buckets and alerts that look like flapping.
sasha: This was introduced in the TS SDK retry change — we set route hint on retry to prefer lower-cost narrowcast. It seemed harmless but we didn't consider telemetry aggregation semantics.
ops-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-2026-0423 (console quota attribution noise) — paging owners.
raj: Short-term: can we dedupe on the server by normalizing routehint for telemetry? Or drop routehint in metrics if token+session match within Xs?
mike: We can normalize on console ingest — prefer the first seen route per token+trace for 2m windows. Cheap and avoids immediate churn.
liz: That helps dashboards but masks real routing differences for customers who actually purposely switch routes. Need to be careful.
sasha: On SDK side: we can stop sending a routehint on retry and instead send an intent flag that doesn't affect route attribution. That requires a minor patch in TS and a follow-up in Go/Py clients to be consistent.
raj: Plan proposal:
- short-term server-side normalization for telemetry (2m window) — rollout today as a console/ingest flag
- medium-term SDK patch: TS v1.2.3 revert auto-routehint-on-retry and add `X-Client-Intent: cost-avoid` (telemetry-safe) — cut canary tomorrow
- long-term: update routing policy to honor explicit route hints only when present at initial request, not on retries (policy change, needs design review)
mike: +1 to that. I'll open the ingest PR and feature flag it. We should add a metric for "normalized attribution" to check for false masking.
liz: Sasha, can you draft the TS patch and a short release note explaining telemetry implications? We need to tell customers who rely on routehint behavior.
sasha: On it. I'll include a code snippet for the opt-out:
```
// new opt-out
client.request({..., retryRouteHint: false})
```
liz: Great. After canary, we should run the quota dashboard smoke test (simulate burst with/without retries) and confirm no flapping.
ops-bot: Note: creating follow-up runbook entry for "quota-attribution-flapping" and linking INC-2026-0423.
raj: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the console flag and watch the dashboards during the TS canary.
mike: tagging @sasha for PR review. :thumbsup:
sasha: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/ts-client/pull/412 — includes tests and migration note. Will coordinate canary channel.
liz: Closing loop: post-canary recap in #eng-platform and also ping support so they can triage any customer tickets.
